issuer: Transport for NSW, through Service NSW
note: Transport for NSW's fees page (fees effective 1 July 2026, read 2026-10-30) gives an unrestricted (gold) licence at $74 for 1 year, $172 for 3 years, $234 for 5 years and $434 for 10 years, all held as terms the holder chooses (the page says the fee depends on how long the licence is renewed for; the 10-year licence is sold only to holders aged 21 to 44, held as its ages, from 21 and under 45), and a photo card for someone with no NSW licence at $68 for 5 years or $122 for 10, both held as terms. A learner licence is had from 16 and, under 25, held at least 12 months before the P1 driving test; the P1 is held 12 months before the P2; the P2 at least 24 months before a full licence: a full licence is kept from 20, the sum of those periods from 16 (a reading). The photo card is for residents over 16, so it is kept from 16. On 2026-10-30 the file was rewritten with the terms the holder chooses among: until then it held the 5-year licence at $234 and the 5-year photo card at $68 only. Later on 2026-10-30 the 10-year licence was given the ages it's sold to; until then the limit was named in this note only.

sources.title: NSW Government, Driver and rider licence fees
sources.said: They depend on the class of licence, the amount of time you renew your licence for, and whether you are a learner or provisional licence holder. ... Unrestricted licence (gold) 1 year: $74 3 years: $172 5 years: $234 10 years: $434 Note: 10-year licences only available for unrestricted licence classes C (car) and/or R (rider), holders age 21 to 44. ... No NSW driver licence 5 years: $68 10 years: $122

sources.title: NSW Government, Provisional P1 licence
sources.said: If you're under 25 – you must also have held your learner licence for at least 12 months ... After you've been on your red Ps for 12 months, you can apply for your green Ps

sources.title: NSW Government, Provisional P2 licence
sources.said: Once you've held your provisional P2 licence for at least 24 months, you can upgrade to a full driver licence .

sources.title: NSW Government, Photo cards
sources.said: proof of address for any resident over the age of 16.
